entries.title: Nike Promo Codes and Discounts: 30% for August 2026
entries.summary: Check out our deals for Nike this August 2026, including 15% off select purchases.
entries.content:
In the midst of our reporting on Nike’s turbulent year, we failed to emphasize one fact: Even as Nike’s corporate leadership flails in a post-Covid world, the company’s shoes and athletic apparel still make up a huge market segment and are still the leading performance models in the industry. Every marathon shoe is just a copy of the iconic Nike Vaporfly, and the Air Force 1 is still one of the top-selling sneakers in the world. You can restock on your own iconic styles with a Nike promo code. Here’s how.

Score 15% Off App Orders With Our Nike Promo Code

Members get rewarded for shopping directly on the Nike app. Once you log on to the app, you’ll automatically become a member. And if you use Nike promo code APP15, you’ll get 15% off your first app purchase and free shipping on orders of $50 or more. So whether you’re in the market for a new pair of Air Jordans or some new leggings for training for your next Marathon, you’ll want to take advantage of this deal.

Celebrate With Nike Coupons For Your Birthday and Member Discounts Everyday

Nike offers a 10% birthday discount when you sign up on the website. You must be a Nike member and logged into your Nike account in order to redeem the discount. The minimum purchase is $100 and applies to the first $500 of a qualifying purchase. You can use it in combination with the Nike free shipping promo codes only. Nike members also receive exclusive access to certain products and member-exclusive sales and discount codes.

Remember earlier when I said Nike members get rewarded? Be sure to become a Nike Member before your birthday month to receive a special birthday Nike discount. Not only will you get that birthday perk, but as a Nike member you’ll also get free shipping on orders of $50 or more, a free 60-day Wear Test to ensure the purchase is right for you, and returns with receipts.

Nike Student Discount Code: 10% Off

All students over 16 in the US, whether you’re in high school, college, or a university, get 10% off at Nike, Nike.com. and in the Nike app. To get the Nike discount code, you’ll just need to verify your student status. To do this, you need to fill out a verification form, verify age, and you may need to provide documentation to verify your status. Once your status is successfully verified, you’ll be sent a single-use Nike promo code for 10% off most items. You’ll just need to make sure you're signed in to your Nike Member profile while using your Nike promo code. This 10% Nike discount code can be used on all sorts of the best Nike apparel and shoes, including the bestselling Nike Vomero Plus men’s running shoes that are full-stack, with ultra-soft max cushioning for enhanced comfort while running.

Nike Discount Programs: Teachers, Military, and Healthcare Works Get 10% Off

There are also other Nike discounts, like 10% off for military and spouses, first responders and medical professionals, and teacher discounts after verification. Check to make sure the items you’re shopping are covered by the discount; certain products, like Nike By You, gift cards, select launch and SNKRS products, and Apple products, are not valid.

Teachers get rewarded with 10% too, just follow the steps for verification status. All military personnel, including active, reservist, veteran, retired US military, and spouses and dependents of active personnel also get 10% off at Nike as a thank you for service. Plus, medical professionals and first responders are also eligible for 10% discounts; that means doctors, nurses, technicians, medical researchers, EMTs, firefighters, and law enforcement.

To get any of these discounts, you’ll need to verify with SheerID, where you’ll receive a single-use promo code that can be used once every seven days. Just be aware, the code expires after two weeks, but you can re-verify your identity to receive a new one.

Support the US Soccer Team With Official Nike Gear

Show off your soccer pride this season with the Team US Soccer x Nike collab. Merchandise from this showy collaboration includes solid, striped, and patterned jerseys for women, men, and children, as well as replica shorts and jerseys from a multitude of favorite players.

Not a US fan? Nike has the fan gear for you too, so you can rep your team, including merch and design collabs from top soccer teams like Norway, France, Brazil, Netherlands, Uruguay, and England.

Get 15% Off the Nike V5 RNR

The Nike V5 RNR just may be the hottest everyday shoe of the season. Stylish enough for streetwear, tough enough to withstand the daily grind, this Y2K inspired shoe has a chunky and lightweight foam midsole. So whether you want a Nike Men’s V5 RNR, women’s, or kid’s, the metallic details and a 3D Swoosh logo blend retro styles with modern sensibilities for an all-around solid shoe.

Trending Nike Styles to Score on Sale Today

Nike still outfits some of the top athletes in the world. If you’re a basketball player, I would say skip the Nike Dunks and get a pair of Kobe Protros like Caitlin Clark. If you’re a runner, Nike recently updated the classic running shoe, the Pegasus. If you’re looking for a low-key street shoe that’s not an Adidas Samba, get the Nike Blazers.

There are tons of Nike’s bestselling shoes on sale right now, including: Nike Dunk Low and Dunk Low Retro SE at 24% off (including multiple under $100 options), 24% off Zoom Vomero 5, 32% off Nike Free Metcon 6, and custom Metcon 10 for as low as $155. Plus, classics are also on sale, with Air Max 270 for up to 30% off, up to 33% off Air Force 1 Low Retro, or Air Force 1 ‘07 LV8 for under $80. Be sure to check out these heavy discounts on tons of Nike styles, from classic to contemporary.

Other Nike Products on Our Radar

Nike got its start as a running company and it still makes the best running apparel on the market. My particular favorites are the firm support, high-waisted ⅞ running leggings (because I’m short) and the running rain jacket, which is also understated enough to wear as an everyday rain jacket. Be sure to check Nike often, with tons of upcoming launches soon to be released. One we’re most excited about is the Team US Collection, inspired by the upcoming Olympic games, with tons of sick US team Olympic apparel. Another hot new release is the Nike SB Dunk Low Pro x Bronx Girls Skate, a cool design inspired by urban landscapes and skate culture.

entries.title: 50% Off DoorDash Promo Code | August 2026
entries.summary: Explore today’s top DoorDash promo codes for $25 off your first order, free delivery, and 50% off DashPass for students and select users.
entries.content:
What can I say about DoorDash to truly encapsulate what this company means to me? I could say it’s the father I never had; it’s the mother I’ve always wanted; the warm embrace of a friend you haven’t seen in a while; the sound of rain as you fall asleep… One of the greatest inventions of the 21st century has been the ability to get virtually any type of food you crave delivered to your front door without having to get up or even speak to another human. We’ve rounded up the best verified DoorDash promo codes, special offers, and free delivery deals.

DoorDash Promo Codes for New Users in 2026

Treat yo’self to staying inside and having your meals delivered to you in the comfort of your own home. Right now, you can get $8 off orders of $25 or more at participating restaurants. As well as a DoorDash promo code for up to $25 off your first order of $30 or more, and you can also get 25% off your first alcohol delivery with DoorDash. Make sure to use DoorDash promo code USDASHTRIAL2Q26 to get the best savings.

Save up to $35 With DoorDash Coupons and This Week’s Deals

Beyond using Doordash promo codes above, you can save more with rotating weekly deals–plus these special offers.

The best coupons include 25% off your entire order, $5 off $20, and 30% off lunchtime delivery. Unlike the many promo codes only for new customers, existing customers can score too, and save 30% (up to $8) for a limited time. Now you have the perfect excuse to get your munch on.

There are also great BOGO deals (who doesn’t love a buy one, get one moment?) like buy 1 get 1 free entrees and a free appetizer when you spend $15 or more, up to $35 off. While discount codes are often only available for your first order, both new and existing customers can take advantage of these coupons. Keep the Deals section in mind to save big with limited-time offers based on your delivery location.

Get 15% Off DoorDash With Our WIRED Code

With this exclusive WIRED DoorDash promo code, first-time customers can get 15% off their first order placed through DoorDash, with savings up to $10 on a $15 minimum order using DoorDash coupon code USEG15OFF2Q26. This DoorDash promo code is only applicable for new customers only and cannot be applied toward alcohol orders.

DoorDash Online Coupons

Depending on your location, you can get personalized DoorDash coupons and DoorDash promo codes specific to your location and local favorites so you can save while revisiting old favorites and new hot spots. There are literally hundreds of top DoorDash promos and new offers that rotate daily for local restaurants, grocery stores, and more. Plus, with DoorDash, you’ll get a $0 delivery fee on eligible orders, free items and discounts on food, deals on groceries, and DashPass member exclusive offers. When I entered my ZIP code, I discovered [DoorDash deals](https://www.doordash.com/en-US/promos) for things like 20% off orders, $5 discounts, and free items on new restaurants I’d never heard of before (my potential new faves?).

Score Free Delivery on Your Next DoorDash Order

DoorDash is the answer to 21st century America's laziness, and was a godsend during the height of the Covid pandemic, when customers could get their favorite foods from restaurants, groceries and household products delivered right to their door without having to leave the safety of their couch. If you’re more of an Uber Eats type of person and haven’t signed up for DoorDash, now is a great time to sign up and get a $0 delivery fee on your first order. Whether you want a romantic night in with your favorite sushi spot across town, or are having a pounding early Sunday morning headache and in desperate need of Advil and Pedialyte from the gas station up the road (not speaking from personal experience or anything), DoorDash has you covered. Go ahead, stay in bed.

DoorDash Student Discount: 50% Off DashPass

Once you’ve signed up and gotten free delivery on your first order, there are still more ways to save. DoorDash has a student discount, where students can receive 50% off a DashPass account. DashPass is a subscription offering unlimited deliveries from 1,000s of eligible restaurants with $0 delivery fees. All you have to do to sign up for student DashPass is verify your student status with Sheer ID. The student DashPass Plan is half off regular DashPass Plans at $4.99 a month or $48 annually.

Get 50% Off and 3 Months of DashPass Free

If you’re not a student, don’t worry, there are tons of other great discounts available at DoorDash. Sign up for DashPass to get $0 delivery fees on orders, 5% back on pickup orders, and tons of other benefits.

If you bank at Chase, Chase cardmembers are eligible for exclusive DashPass benefits on DoorDash and Caviar when an eligible Chase credit card is added to their account. Chase is offering 3 months of Dash Pass free, plus 50% off the next 9 months of service.

Whether you're wanting to go to tried-and-true chains for burgers and pizza like McDonald’s, Shake Shack, or Domino’s, or some true, authentic Mexican like Chipotle or Taco Bell (I kid! Don’t come for me), DoorDash is a great way to eat through the world without ever leaving your couch.

DoorDash Delivery Updates and New Features in 2026

DoorDash has some really exciting updates happening, including the launch of their Going Out program, a new dine-in program for customers starting first in NYC and Miami. With this program, diners will be able to book restaurant reservations directly through the DoorDash app, and will get rewarded for their loyalty by earning exclusive offers when dining in, as well as earning rewards for regular visits to favorite spots. Plus, DashPass members will get even more exclusive perks and in-store rewards. Check it out for yourself—explore the new “Going Out” tab in the DoorDash app, redeem exclusive in-store offers, and earn rewards for repeat visits. Customers save an average of $9 when using these perks.

DoorDash is also launching DoorDash Dot, a robot that delivers food to you rather than humans. Which seems like a great idea. (Note the thick layer of sarcasm, reader.) The scary glimpse into our future continues as creators are rewarded. Short-form videos from local creators and foodies are now live in the DoorDash app; DoorDash hopes that consumers will be able preview dishes before they order, to more accurately see things like preparation style and portion size. This is starting in Atlanta, Austin, Miami and San Francisco, with more rolling out through the end of the year.

Give the Gift of a DoorDash Gift Card

Not sure what to get your loved ones for their next birthday or holiday? A DoorDash gift card is the gift that never misses. Whether you want to lift the burden of planning dinners for new parents, or have a friend who’s always ordering takeout, a DoorDash gift card can be a thoughtful way to be there for your loved one when you physically can’t. There are tons of different gift card styles, brands, and types, so you can rest assured there’s a gift for every occasion and person.

How to Save With Your DoorDash Crimson Card

Dashers can get extra rewards on top of what was mentioned above with the DoorDash Crimson Card. With this special card, you’ll be able to get paid instantly after every dash (no more waiting for weeks), get cash back on purchases made using the card, and manage finances through the Dasher app. With the Crimson Card, Dashers have the choice to get paid instantly and automatically with no deposit fees after every dash or get rewards like cash back on gas. If you’re a Dasher and want to apply for DoorDash Crimson, just tap the 'Earnings' tab, and then 'Learn More' in your Dasher app to apply.

Unlock Exclusive DoorDash Discounts When You Become a Dasher

Looking for a new job with flexibility or a side gig? If you become a DoorDash Dasher, you can get major benefits. Whether you’re biking, driving, or delivering full-time, Dasher discounts can help you save as you earn money with deliveries. Dashers can access exclusive discounts from things like gas and auto care, to health benefits, phone plans, and tax tools. Plus, Dashers can save even more on purchases and get rewards with the DoorDash Crimson Visa Debit Card.

How to Save With Your DoorDash Crimson Card

Dashers can get extra rewards on top of what was mentioned above with the DoorDash Crimson Card. With this special card, you’ll be able to get paid instantly after every dash (no more waiting for weeks), get cash back on purchases made using the card, and manage finances through the Dasher app. With the Crimson Card, Dashers have the choice to get paid instantly and automatically with no deposit fees after every dash or get rewards like cash back on gas. If you’re a Dasher and want to apply for DoorDash Crimson, just tap the 'Earnings' tab, and then 'Learn More' in your Dasher app to apply.

entries.title: Office Depot Coupons: Save With Promo Codes in August 2026
entries.summary: From furniture and ink to professional printing services, use an Office Depot discount code to maximize your savings on every workspace essential.
entries.content:
As someone who WFH for a minimum of forty hours a week, and is constantly rotating between working from an office chair, couch, and bed, I can truly say that the office furniture you use matters. Not only can it make or break your body (literally), it also helps to have office supplies and furniture to get you in the professional state of mind when at home.

We love Office Depot’s wide selection of office chairs and standing desks to outfit our home offices. Plus, Office Depot has a great selection of home printers for every price point and need, with options from our favorite brands like Epson and HP. Outfitting a home office or providing office supplies no matter where you work can be overwhelming and costly. Luckily, Office Depot has everything a business needs, from staples to paper to shelving and scanners. These costs can add up quickly, and that’s why we have rounded up some of the best Office Depot coupons to help you save big.

Get the Best Office Depot Back to School Deals

The early bird gets the worm, and although the start of the school year is several months away, you can save big on school supplies and essentials when you buy early. Office Depot school supplies have hundreds of supplies for under three dollars, in-store pick up available in minutes, and a handy school landing page where everything is categorized to make it easy to shop by grade, need, and price range. There are deals for 20% off JanSport backpacks, $98 Texas Instruments graphing calculators, BOGO deals on Sharpies, Scotch tape, Post-Its, and more essentials, and tons more deals (too many to include here!)

Save $20 on Your Next $100 Purchase

These days, it’s easy to spend $100. Whether that’s for a budget printer or a whole bunch of pens and paper clips, you can save money on purchases you were already going to make with this Office Depot promo code. Right now, you can get $20 off a purchase of $100 or more. Once you’re done shopping and have all of the items in your cart, input the Office Depot coupon code YES20 in the box at the payment screen to get the Office Depot discount. Perhaps best of all, this Office Depot discount code applies to all regular-priced items across valuable home office categories like furniture, supplies, and tech. Be sure to act soon; this offer expires on June 27.

$40 Off Instantly With an Office Depot Coupon Code

If you need to upgrade your organizational system or get a new chair that doesn’t trigger back spasms, now’s a great time to invest in your home office setup for less. With this Office Depot promo code, you can get $40 off when you purchase $200 or more (an easy milestone to get to). To get this discount, input Office Depot promo code YES40 at checkout for massive savings on a myriad of regularly-priced items. This Office Depot discount is only good until June 27, so I’d use it sooner rather than later.

Get a Free $50 Prepaid Visa Reward Card

If you’re wanting to upgrade your office furniture, like a luxe office chair, gaming chair, or standing desk, now’s a great time to make an investment in your home office. Get rewarded for the larger purchases you were already going to make. When you spend $500 at Office Depot right now, you’ll get a free $50 prepaid Visa Reward Card (until May 23). This offer excludes products from HP, Samsung, Canon, Epson, Brother, Lexmark, Microsoft Surface, Google hardware, simplehuman, postage stamps, ink and toner. This offer isn’t valid in Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, or the Virgin Islands, and there’s a limit of one per household or business. This $50 reward Office Depot coupon code will be automatically applied and will be reflected during checkout, with no Office Depot promo code needed.

Office Depot Printing Coupons: Professional Projects With Office Depot

If you’re a small business owner, you can get deep discounts on business cards, banners, marketing materials, and basically everything needed to promote and get your business off the ground. We have a myriad of rotating Office Depot printing coupons (primarily aimed at business cards) so you can level up your branding, with no Office Depot coupon code needed to get steep discounts on professional printing.

Save on Printer Supplies With Office Depot Ink Coupons

We can put a man on the moon, we can clone sheep. But somehow, home office printers have been stuck in the dark ages. Huge, clunky, and prone to error messages and hardware issues, printers have become a relic of the past, with many at a loss for where to get the best.

As digital tickets and phone camera scanning become increasingly common, more homes are operating without a printer. However, if you have moved into your home office or need one for your business, buying printer supplies and ink in bulk from Office Depot is a great way to save some money on these annoying purchases. You can get recycling rewards and bundle deals on HP and Epson ink with these Office Depot ink coupons for HP printers. These Office Depot promo codes can help save on multi-pack cartridges, along with “subscribe and save” options for automated, recurring ink deliveries at an even lower price point.

Unlock 40% Off All Photo Products

If you’re looking for a great personal gift, or want to finally hang up those family portraits, now’s a great time to get all of your photo printing and photo gifts needs met for way less, with this 40% off Office Depot promo (until August 22). This means 40% off all photo products—perfect for custom gift ideas, invitations, greeting cards, and portraits for the home. With Office Depot Photo Services, you’ll be able to choose your favorite photos and turn them into a myriad of personalized products and gifts, like canvas prints, large format posters, photo books, cards, invitations, and photo calendars. Plus, Office Depot has other perks, like same day and/or next day photo products which are available tomorrow if you order by 2 pm, as well as next-day custom cards, calendars, invitations, and announcements.

entries.title: Columbia Promo Codes: 15% Off | August 2026
entries.summary: Explore current Columbia deals on jackets, outdoor gear, and apparel. Find active Columbia promo codes, student discounts, and free shipping offers to save on your next adventure.
entries.content:
When I decided to take a last-minute ski trip, despite never having skied before, I went straight to Columbia. Was I shredding the slopes? Absolutely not, but at least I was warm, thanks to my Snowy Summit Insulated Jacket and Bugaboo II Pants. Here at WIRED, we’re fans of Columbia. The brand makes reliable, well-priced outdoor gear for skiing, hiking, hunting, or just a day at the beach. Plus, there’s almost always a deal to be found.

WIRED reviewer Chris Haslam loves the Columbia Konos Trillium ATR as a value all-around trail-running shoe for faster hikes, day trips, and mixed terrain excursions. The plush cushioning and 8-millimeter drop are ideal on packed dirt, gravel, and woodland paths. For hiking boots, he recommends the Tellurix Titanium OutDry, which are waterproof, offer serious traction on wet rock and mud, and are surprisingly lightweight at 1.6 pounds per pair.

With summer approaching, now’s the time to prepare for outings, and if you’re eyeing snow gear, the off-season is when prices hit their lowest. I’ve gathered the latest Columbia promo codes to sweeten the deal.

Don’t Miss the Columbia Summer Sale

Although we’re in peak camping season right now, it’s still not too late to upgrade your gear for the rest of the season and beyond. Take advantage of the Columbia Summer Sale and get outfitted for your next adventure for less, with discounts of $30 and more on ​​men’s, women’s, and kid’s apparel, as well as shoes, accessories, and equipment. So whether you want to snag a packable Women's Pouration II Jacket for 50% off, or a Men's Strata Trail Low Waterproof Shoe for 40% off, there’s a Columbia discount for all of your outdoor adventure essentials.

Columbia Promo Code: 15% Off All Orders

Join Columbia’s Greater Rewards program—it’s free to sign up and you won’t need a Columbia promo code—to get 15% off your first online order. Note, this particular coupon can’t be combined with any other Columbia discount code or deal and expires if not redeemed within 30 days of the date of issuance. Plus, as a member, you’ll earn points on purchases, get free standard shipping, and receive a 20 percent discount on your birthday.

Unlock Columbia Discount Codes and Get $20 off

Once you sign up for Columbia’s Greater Rewards program and opt in for email notifications, you’ll acquire a unique Columbia coupon code for $10 off your online purchase when you spend $100 or more. If you subscribe to both email and text notifications, the single-use Columbia coupon will increase to $20 off your purchase of $100 or more.

Top Columbia Deals for Current Students

Columbia offers a 10% discount for students and teachers. You must log in to ID.me and verify your status to receive the Columbia promo code.

Columbia Military Discount: 10% Off

Active and retired military members, as well as first responders, are also eligible for a 10% discount. You must log in directly to ID.me and verify your status to receive the Columbia promo code.

Get Free Shipping With Columbia Codes

As a Greater Rewards member, you get free standard shipping on all online orders, with no minimum purchase requirement. As long as you’re signed into your account, the Columbia free shipping code will automatically be applied at checkout.

Give More With the Columbia Gift Card

Not sure what to get the adventurer in your life? If your loved one is a nature enthusiast, you need a great grad gift idea for someone taking their gap year, or the giftee is finally taking that backpacking trip, a Columbia gift card can be a thoughtful gift for many occasions. A Columbia gift card is a practical way to keep friends and family warm, dry, cool, and protected outdoors—and they can pick out what they want themselves, so you’re not left guessing. It’s also super easy to do: you pick out the design online and send them instantly by email.

How to Apply Your Columbia Coupon Code

So you’ve snagged a Columbia coupon code. Congrats! You’re on your way to big savings. There are two ways to use your Columbia promo code: you can see the first after you click on “Apply Promo Code or Discount” under the “order summary” tab. The second option will be shown during billing when you checkout, you’ll just need to click on the “Have a Promo Code or Gift Card?” text that lives right above where you enter card information during checkout. That’s it! Just ensure that the Columbia coupon code is entered exactly as it appears, including capitalization and hyphens.

entries.title: Dyson Promo Codes: 25% Off in August 2026
entries.summary: Get 25% off with a Dyson coupon code, plus save up to $600 with discounts on vacuums, $150 off Airwraps, and more.
entries.content:
If you’re hunting for a new vacuum, Dyson has surely come up in one way or another. The brand is famous for its powerful vacuum cleaners, but its air power also extends to other parts of the home, including hair care and air purification. It’s a dream household staple; I lugged around an old Dyson vacuum for years until I could upgrade to one of the newer stick models rather than buying something that wouldn’t be as powerful or last as long.

But the cost can make it a hard investment to make, even if it’s worth it. If you’re shopping for one of Dyson’s long-lasting gadgets but have a limited budget, fear not: we’ve got coupon codes to make it a better buy, plus tips on how to get discounts on Dyson’s website. Read on to get all of our Dyson promo codes and coupons, and learn the best ways to shop for a Dyson.

Get a 15% Off Dyson Promo Code When You Register

Usually, you need to be a new customer to get a great discount, but Dyson actually rewards you for being a repeat customer. You can get 15% off your next order by registering your current Dyson product’s serial number.

Sign Up to Unlock a 10% Off Dyson Coupon Code

You can also get 10 percent off your next Dyson purchase without needing a device to register. You’ll want to sign up your mobile number using a pop-up on Dyson’s homepage. That will get you a text, and you’ll have to reply with “Y” to officially register. After you reply, you’ll get a message with a link that will reveal a single-use code for 10 percent off your next purchase at Dyson.

You can also sign up for texts or Dyson’s email newsletters (like this hair care newsletter) to get access to exclusive Dyson sale events, more coupon codes, and new product releases (and several new vacuums are due out this year).

Save up to $600 With This Week’s Dyson Coupons

Dyson always has sales going on its website at the Dyson Deals Hub. The discounts rotate weekly, and there’s always different active coupons in different categories of Dyson products. You might find a nice discount on the V12 vacuum, for instance, or the Dyson Airstrait.

Keep Cool for Less: $130 Off the Dyson Cool CF1

Summer’s in full effect and the sun just keeps blazing. The Dyson Cool CF1 is the high-tech, clean air solution you’ve been looking for. Using Dyson’s Air Multiplier projection, this sleek fan is made for quiet (including sleep mode), powerful cooling. Usually $380, it’s $130 off, now only $250—a sweet deal for summer. Dyson’s known for their sleek, futuristic designs and this fan is no different. It has no blades, which means no choppy air flow, dust collection, or hassling with potentially dangerous blades while cleaning. The annular aperture accelerates air, drawing in surrounding air to project smooth, uninterrupted airflow. The model is also energy efficient, and has a wide ange of oscillation angles and manual tilt for precise cooling wherever you are.

Save 30% When You Shop the Dyson Outlet

Looking for a bigger discount? Try Dyson’s outlet of refurbished vacuums, hair tools, and air purifiers. Youl’l find discounts of up to 30 percent off the original price, and each one is inspected, restored to like-new condition, and backed by Dyson’s official warranty. It’s a good way to get a great discount on products like the Supersonic hair dryers, which you can find for under $200 when refurbished, and Dyson’s multi-stylers can be found for under $300. These do have a shorter warranty period than new products, though; it’ll only be six months to a year rather than two to five years.

Dyson Discount: 20% Off

During the Dyson owner savings event, Dyson owners get rewarded by getting 20% off Dyson technology purchases. When you choose one of the qualifying floorcare or air purifiers, you’ll add your one-time-use code at the payment section when you checkout online at Dyson. Or if you’d rather, you can simply log in and your Dyson discount will automatically be applied at checkout. Plus, if you’d rather, you can also shop at your nearest Dyson Demo Store or make a purchase over the phone. And if you don’t have a Dyson discount code automatically, you can register your machine by calling 1-866-693-9766 to speak to a Dyson expert about Owner Rewards.

Get the Best Offers at Dyson Week

If you’re wanting to invest in this oftentimes pricey, lifetime-lasting technology, I’d suggest looking at the Dyson deals webpage, where you can see all of the exclusive rotating Dyson offers available right now and shop by category, like cordless vacuums, hair care, air treatment, headphones, and more. Some of the best deals I’ve seen so far have been for the viral Dyson Airwrap Origin multi-styler and dryer, which has three attachments and is $150 off right now, and the V12 Detect Slim, a highly-rated cordless Dyson vacuum with 60 minutes of run time for $250 off.

Unlock the Best Dyson Airwrap Promos

Like all of Dyson’s tech lineup, Dyson hair tools have the signature high-power, efficiency, sleek design, … and high price tag. One of Dyson’s most iconic and history-withstanding tools is the Dyson Airwrap, which debuted back in 2018. We rated it a 9/10 WIRED Recommends, for its multifunctionality, different offerings for different hair types, less heat use than previous models, and light and easy-to-use design.

When it comes to hair gadgets, there are many gimmicks that claim to make styling easy and effortless, but the Dyson Airwrap actually works, using air to suck strands of your hair around the curling barrels to produce a lasting result without subjecting your hair to too much damaging heat. It's a multifunction styler, but the Airwrap really shines as a curling iron. Using its internal motor, it creates a vortex of air inside the hollow barrel powerful enough to draw your hair to it. All you have to do is place the end of your hair near the barrel, and the machine does the gripping and wrapping for you, so you don't have to worry about touching a hot curling barrel.

Dyson Purifier Deal: $150 Off

I’m of the opinion that everyone needs an air purifier and a fan. So why not combine both? (Especially if you are short on space like me.) We at WIRED love the Dyson Purifier Cool PC2 which works in tandem to powerfully cool with purified air. Not only does it work as a fan to blow cool air, it also captures gases and 99% of pollutants to redistribute cool, purified air throughout your home for a healthier living space. It also conveniently connects to the MyDyson app for hands-free control anywhere, and it’s $100 off right now.

entries.title: It Looks Like Nothing Can Dent MAGA’s Support for ICE
entries.summary: Despite weeks of renewed press coverage and controversy around ICE, Donald Trump’s supporters appear to be standing by the agency no matter what.
entries.content:
On Tuesday, the day after hundreds of thousands of Haitian migrants effectively lost their temporary protected status that allowed them to live and work in the US, Republican pundit Steve Bannon wasted little time in demanding their instant removal.

“I was under the assumption that when they pulled TPS and their eligibility for that program ended … they were going to be boarding planes or buses today … today, this morning at dawn to go back to Haiti,” said Bannon, a longtime ally of President Donald Trump, on his War Room podcast on Tuesday. “Why are they not out of the country?”

Mike Davis, a conservative political strategist agreed with Bannon: “The solution is to get these people the hell out of our country as fast as possible, and that includes these Haitians.”

White nationalist Nick Fuentes, who has been a vocal critic of Trump’s deportation policies because he doesn’t find them extreme enough, called Haitians “the worst of the worst” and “very low IQ people” on his Rumble show Tuesday night.

In a Telegram channel run by the Proud Boys of Columbus, one member posted a clip of the song “I’m Walking on Sunshine” alongside the news about the revoking of temporary protected status. “They gotta go back,” the member wrote.

It’s been a while since shock-and-awe tactics from Immigration and Customs Enforcement first gained national notoriety. For months, figures like former Border Patrol leader Greg Bovino terrorized cities like Minneapolis and Chicago. But since replacing former Department of Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem with Markwayne Mullin—derisively referred to by Bannon as the “Kung fu plumber”—ICE’s operations have shrunk into the shadows, though the agency’s deportation and arrest numbers have remained astronomical.

In recent weeks, things are boiling over again.

Earlier this month, an ICE agent shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, Texas. Araujo had lived in the country for 35 years, had three children, and owned his own business. Just days later, another ICE agent killed Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine. Both men were shot while in their vehicles. ICE, as WIRED has revealed, is also tracking its critics online, using data brokers to “identify unaccompanied minors,” and working to prevent state health inspectors from reviewing its network of detention centers. On Tuesday, The New York Times reported that the Trump administration was now targeting immigrants at airports whose visas have expired, or are in a transition status, arresting spouses of American citizens.

Even so, Steve Bannon and the other Republican pundits aren’t alone: Support for ICE among Trump’s most loyal supporters remains incredibly high, with 74 percent of people who identify as MAGA Republicans professing confidence in ICE, according to a YouGov poll published last week. The same poll shows that 80 percent of MAGA Republicans oppose abolishing ICE.

The YouGov findings were backed up by another poll published last week by the Public Religion Research Institute , which found that three-quarters of Republicans had a positive view of ICE, would be in favor of more funding for the agency, and disagreed that ICE was making communities less safe. The poll also found that 73 percent of Republicans are in support of internment camps to hold “immigrants who are in the country illegally” until they can be deported.

The YouGov poll also found that just 51 percent of Republicans had, in the week of the shootings, read, seen, or heard anything about immigrants being shot and killed by ICE agents. What they may have seen however is Trump’s Truth Social post around the same time. In the post, Trump appeared to overrule an internal ICE memo telling agents to suspend vehicle stops, after a furious response from his MAGA base. He also told his supporters that ICE was “loved and respected in America.”

Much of his base thinks that deportations are actually not happening fast enough. ICE is on track to deport 458,000 individuals this year according to its own data, a colossal figure that still falls well short of the 1 million deportations Trump promised shortly after his inauguration. (This, in the words of border czar Tom Homan, is what the administration calls “deportation-maxxing.”)

Americans have been caught in the dragnet as well, as ICE’s actions have resulted in widespread civil rights violations, according to a report published this month by the American Civil Liberties Union, which found that across eight states, ICE agents targeted 155 US citizens, 32 of whom were children, during the first year of Trump’s second term. Previous research from UC Berkeley found that half of all the people ICE has arrested had no criminal records, despite the administration claiming to be deporting the “worst of the worst.” Federal agents have shot and killed four people, including two US citizens.

On the other hand, the majority of Americans believe ICE has used too much force, according to YouGov, and as a result have little or no confidence in the agency. Almost half of Americans believe it's time for ICE to be abolished.

What these polls show is that while America as a whole is rejecting Trump’s immigration policies, his base is almost completely supportive. And rather than distancing themselves from ICE’s actions, Republicans seem to be leaning in again, even spending more money and running more ads about immigration than Democrats, NPR reported last week.

With just months left before the midterms offer voters a chance to have their say on these policies, Republicans are gambling that their base doesn’t actually want ICE going anywhere. In November, the country will see if they’re right.

This is an edition of Hugo Lowell’s Inner Loop newsletter. Read previous newsletters here.

entries.title: Save Up to $100 on Apple’s Newest AirPods (2026)
entries.summary: Save up to $100 on Apple’s latest AirPods models before prices go back up.
entries.content:
If you’ve been patiently waiting for a discount on Apple’s latest earbuds or over-ear headphones, it’s finally here. For a limited time, both the AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2 are on sale, knocking up to $100 off their regular prices. Whether you want pocketable earbuds for everyday use, premium noise-canceling headphones, or seamless Apple integration, these are some of the best prices I've seen since launch. As always with Amazon deals, there's no telling how long they'll stick around, so I wouldn't wait too long if you've been planning to upgrade.

For more recommendations, check out our guides to the Best Noise-Canceling Headphones, Best Wireless Earbuds, and the Best Headphones for Working Out.

Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

Apple AirPods Pro 3 for $200 ($49 Off)

The latest AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s best AirPods yet. Upgrades include stronger noise canceling, a new acoustic architecture for deeper bass, and redesigned ear tips for a more secure fit. New tools include a built-in heart rate sensor for fitness tracking, live translation, and a camera remote to snap photos or videos on your iPhone. These earbuds are also the first AirPods to be IP57 rated against dust, sweat, and rain.

Right now, they are 20 percent off at Amazon, Target, and Walmart. There’s no telling how long this discount will last, so I’d grab a pair now if they’re on your wish list.

Apple AirPods Max 2 for $449 ($100 Off)

The AirPods Max 2 are arguably the most stylish pair of noise-canceling headphones on the market. The newer H2 chip improves active noise cancellation and transparency mode and enables a suite of intelligent features, including conversation awareness, live translation, and improved Siri interactions. The AirPods Max 2 are designed with a new high-dynamic-range amplifier for deeper bass, more natural vocals, and cleaner highs.

At $549, the AirPods Max 2 can be a tough sell, especially with so many excellent, more affordable alternatives on the market. But $100 off, they’re a lot easier to justify, especially if you want the seamless integration that comes with Apple’s ecosystem. It’s unclear how long this deal will last, so I’d snag a pair sooner rather than later if you’ve been eyeing them.

entries.title: Which of Dyson’s 2026 Vacuum Models Is the Best?
entries.summary: Curious if you should get Dyson’s new 2026 stick vacuums or stick to the older ones? I tested five models, old and new, to find out for you.
entries.content:
Dyson's vacuum lineup has a whole new look these days, but that doesn't necessarily make it easier to decide if you're looking to buy one.

The Dyson V16 Piston Animal ($980), V10 Konical ($500), and V8 Cyclone ($400) arrived to change up Dyson's cordless vacuum options. The older V15 Detect ($650) and Gen5Detect ($800) are also still available and great vacuums, which raises the question: Should you upgrade? Which Dyson model is worth the cash with so many options (and widely ranging price points) to choose from?

I tested all five of these vacuums against each other in a series of tests to see which ones stood out among the pack. The two overall winners? The Gen5Detect was the number one winner, with the V16 Piston Animal right behind it, and the V10 Konical coming up third even though it's a much cheaper option. Read on to find out which model did best in each test, what the stats look like for each Dyson vacuum, and how I scored the final results.

Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.

Top 3 Performers

A Quick Dyson Vacuum Rundown

Dyson's naming convention is fun, and the numbers usually represent which models are more powerful or offer better accessories, but not always. Most of its vacuums have the V name, which, to my best guess, simply stands for “vacuum.” The numbers aren't always in order of release and usually reflect a vacuum's power level and capabilities. The V10 and V8 have the same power level but different heads, for example, while the V16 is more powerful than the V15. But not all vacuums are named the same; the Gen5Detect has a different name entirely, and falls in between the V15 and V16 when it comes to suction power and price tag.

Here's a quick chart to understand the power levels and compatible accessories that differentiate each vacuum from the other. You might also spot things like “Plus” or “Total” when you're shopping for a Dyson vacuum, and that usually reflects the attachments included with the vacuum.

Model Suction Power Vacuum Heads Included Accessories Filter Add-Ons Dyson V8 Cyclone ($400) 150 air watts Digital Motorbar Crevice tool Whole-machine filtration None at this time Dyson V10 Konical ($500) 150 air watts All Floor Cones Crevice tool, mini motorized tool HEPA Auto-emptying Dok Dyson V15 Detect ($650) 240 air watts Digital Motorbar, Fluffy Optic Crevice tool, mini motorized tool Whole-machine filtration Submarine head Dyson Gen5Detect ($800) 262 air watts Digital Motorbar, Fluffy Optic Hair screw tool, Combination tool, and Dusting and crevice tool (built-in) HEPA None at this time Dyson V16 Piston Animal ($980) 315 air watts All Floor Cones Sense, Fluffy Optic Hair screw tool 2.0, crevice tool, built-in crevice tools HEPA Submarine head, docking station planned

This gives you a pretty easy look at what you're getting for each model. As the models increase in number (both in the name and in the price tag), the vacuum usually gains more accessories or cleaner heads, more air watts of suction power, and sometimes the option to add the Submarine wet cleaner head on for an additional price, or future compatibility with Dyson's Auto-empty Dok station that's coming out soon.

The Digital Motorbar and All Floor Cones cleaner heads are both compatible with soft and hard floors, which is why sometimes it's the only head included. More expensive Dyson models will also include the Fluffy Optic cleaner head, which is designed specifically for hard floors and has an illuminated light to help you spot dust and debris. The All Floor Cones cleaner head includes a light too, so you're able to get that feature on both the V16 and V10 without switching heads.

Here are the tests I ran for each vacuum, and which ones did best—and worst.

Sand Test

BEST: V10 Konical ($500)

WORST: V8 Cyclone ($400)

I tested all five Dyson models on a small black rug onto which I poured fine, white sand to see how well it was vacuumed up. The best was the V10 Konical, followed by the V15 Detect. Both left a small trail of sand behind in different spots, which makes sense since they have different head designs, but the V10's trail was smaller than the V15's, with a small line in the middle compared to the larger trail the V15 had on its right side.

The V8, meanwhile, stalled entirely when I tried to use it on the rug and couldn't vacuum up sand whatsoever. It weirdly seemed to have an issue with the thin rug, even though equally or more powerful vacuums were able to vacuum on it.

Both Gen5Detect and V16 Piston Animal were able to vacuum on the thin rug, but the stronger suction also kept trying to take the rug with it, giving both mixed results and leaving a lot of sand behind on each pass. I retested both of these on a thicker rug in case the suction level wasn't a match for the thin rug, and both did much better, but the Gen5Detect did the best, getting every bit of sand in one swoop. The V16 got most of its sand, but pushed some sand into a little pile in front of itself.

Cereal Test

BEST: Gen5Detect ($800)

WORST: None

When I last did a cereal test, I used a cornflake-style cereal. This time I switched to the cereal I know many parents like myself are much more likely to have all over the floors: Cheerios. I crushed up several in my hand and dropped those along with full Cheerios onto my thicker living room rug. Overall, every Dyson did a good job cleaning this up on the first pass.

The results on this one had pretty minimal differences for these models. The V8, V10, and V15 Detect all usually got the Cheerios and pieces on the first run, sending one to three pieces flying while it did so, but not so far away you wouldn't get to vacuum them up. The Gen5Detect sent nothing flying, though, so it pulls slightly ahead. The V16 sent only a single tiny piece flying forward. But it was right behind the Gen5Detect out of these Dyson models.

Litter Test

BEST: Gen5Detect ($800)

WORST: V8 Cyclone ($400)

Next, I tested these vacuums against a thing I vacuum the most off my vinyl plank floors: cat litter. For this test, since it was on a hard surface instead of a rug, I switched the vacuums' heads to the Fluffy Optic cleaner head when available. That's only on the V15, V16, and Gen5Detect, so those heads changed while the other two models still used the Digital Motorbar (V8) or the All Floor Cones (V10) heads they came with.

It's no surprise that the two standouts both had a Fluffy Optic head. The Gen5Detect left the cleanest floor behind, with not a spec of litter dust to be found from the vacuum's illuminated light after a single pass. The V16 Piston Animal mostly did well, leaving no litter behind, but it did push a small amount of litter in front of itself, similar to the sand test. This only happened in a pass of extremely thick litter, so more day-to-day litter cleanup shouldn't have this issue. Still, the Gen5Detect pulls slightly ahead once again.

The V15 is right behind these two, but left a little dust behind that I could see with the Fluffy Optic's headlight (though no large pieces, and it looked just as clean to the naked eye). Meanwhile, the V10 Konical did fine enough, but needed two passes to get all the debris. The V8 landed last after it pulled a similar move when vacuuming sand and simply pushed the litter into a pile in front of itself, so I then had to move the vacuum on top of and around to vacuum it up, and it took a few passes to do so.

Handheld Test

BEST: V16 Piston Animal ($980) and Gen5Detect ($800)

WORST: V15 Detect ($650)

Dyson's vacuums function nicely as a handheld vacuum, no matter the model. I tested all five models on my carpeted stairs, and I'd recommend any one of them if that's a big use in your household. The V16 and Gen5Detect pull ahead for me because you can really feel the higher suction at work when you're in handheld mode, and both vacuums showed serious results afterward of dustbins filled with new hair and dust. Especially as a cat owner and a parent of a small child, the carpeted stairs around my house have a lot of debris worked into them. Plus, both of these vacuums have built-in crevice tools you can use in handheld mode, but the V16's will always stay attached, while you need to remove the Gen5's to attach the head directly to the handheld motor.

The V15 also did a fine job, but it felt like it was gliding over my stairs rather than locking into the carpet like the other Dyson vacuums. Even the V8 and V10 with lower power levels felt more suctioned into my carpet than the V15 did for me during my handheld stair testing. Both those cheaper models fell into the runner-up range for me with this test.

Carpet and Rug Test

BEST: Gen5Detect ($800) and V10 Konical ($500)

WORST: V15 Detect ($650)

Originally, I tested an early release version of the V16 Piston Animal that had some clogging issues on carpet. But after getting a current release model, the V16 did much better overall. Both the V16 and the Gen5Detect did an impressive job on my carpets and rugs, and pulled an impressive amount of cat hair and dust out of my recently vacuumed carpets. These both have different heads, but the powerful suction really comes into play on carpet more than anywhere else, especially if you have pets.

Meanwhile, the V10 Konical has the All Floor Cones cleaner head that glided nicely on carpet. The V10's head was a little easier to push around than the Digital Motorbar head (which both the V8 and V15 have) on rugs. The V8 Cyclone took the most effort to push around on my rug, but moved much better on carpet.

The V15 Detect was similar, but unlike the rest of these vacuums, it has a trigger button instead of a power button. That means you have to keep that engaged the entire time when doing a longer vacuuming session. The rest of these vacuums have a power button you click instead, so I don't love the trigger for longer vacuuming sessions. If you're a big vacuumer or have a home with a large amount of carpet, you're going to want a power button, and likely one of the higher-suction vacuums.

Which One Wins?

The results, as you can tell above, are a little murky. The higher-suction vacuums usually took home the prize in most categories, but the V10 Konical was a surprisingly solid all-around performer. To find my winner, I put all of my tests and Dyson models into a chart and scored them on a 1 to 4 point scale, allowing 4 points if the vacuum did the best, 1 if the worst, and a 2 or 3 depending on how middle-of-the-road the results were. One vacuum had a nice lead with a near-perfect score of 19 points.

The biggest standout from these tests was the Gen5Detect. It came out of these tests with a near-perfect score after the five rounds of testing. It does a great job with its level of powerful suction, and it transitions well between most kinds of debris. As a pet owner, I especially like it for carpet, since the 280 air watts do a great job pulling out hair and pet dander from deep in the carpet. I've actually filled up this vacuum's debris tank before after vacuuming only a few days before with a weaker option.

It's one of the most expensive for a reason, and comes with more attachments than any other model. I do find myself regularly grabbing the Fluffy Optic head for vacuuming my hard floors, which cover many square feet of my home. If you're looking to really splurge on the best vacuum, this is still the one to get.

The only downside is compatibility with Dyson's bigger attachments, namely a mop head or docking station. It doesn't have a Submarine option like the V16 or V15, and Dyson's Auto-empty Dok won't work with this model. But if you aren't worried about add-ons, this is the vacuum to buy. It's had better sales since the launch of the new models, too.

The V16 Piston Animal's powerful 315 air watts of suction did pretty well on almost every test. My only issue with this vacuum compared to the Gen5Detect is that it was more likely to push small debris (in my tests, both sand and litter) into a pile in front of itself if you were vacuuming a large spill. Gen5Detect did better all around, but the V16 Piston Animal stayed close behind that hiccup.

It's a powerful all-around vacuum with some nice design upgrades to make it a little easier to use. This newer model has a release below the vacuum motor to release the cleaner head without having to bend down, and built-in crevice tools to both the handheld motor and the long wand that makes up the middle of the device. There's also a compressor to help push dust out of the dustbin, and it'll be compatible with Dyson's upcoming self-emptying docking station. There's also a Submarine version ($1,100) so you can use this vacuum as a mop, too.

It has some nice quality-of-life upgrades, but it's really expensive. I'd recommend it if you know you also want to invest in the mop head and docking station; otherwise, just get the Gen5Detect.

One of the best overall performers is nearly half the price of my winners. The Dyson V10 Konical never once scored in last place, and was especially comfortable to use on carpets and rugs with the new cleaner head design. It did much better than the more expensive and powerful Gen5Detect and V15 Detect when vacuuming up sand, and I found it more comfortable to push around than the Digital Motorbar head on the V15 and V8 when it came to vacuuming a low-pile rug.

It didn't do as well on hard floors, but it didn't do poorly, either. This cheaper model comes with just the single head, but if you don't want to spend the better part of a grand, I'd rather only have this head than the Digital Motorbar head. The All Floor Cones cleaner head also has a built-in light, which you won't get on cheaper or older models. Plus, it'll be compatible with the self-emptying docking station Dyson has coming out soon. For the price point, it's a fantastic buy.

Also Consider: The Upgrade Options

BEST: V16 Piston Animal Submarine ($1,100) and V10 Konical with Auto-empty Dok ($650)

WORST: V8 Cyclone ($400) and Gen5Detect ($800)

I'm putting this section after the testing because if you're just looking for a good vacuum, this might not be relevant for you. But there are some interesting upgrades with certain Dyson models you might want to consider, which might sway you toward a certain model over the testing aspects—like if you want a stick vacuum that can work with a self-emptying docking station, or one that can double as a mop. Not all of Dyson's vacuums can do these things, but some of them can—and one can do both.

Both the V16 Piston Animal and the V15 Detect have a Submarine variant (that retail for $1,100 and $750, respectively) that will give you the Submarine head along with the rest of the vacuum accessories. They have slightly different designs, but both are a wet roller head that stores both clean and dirty water while being powered by the motor in the rest of the vacuum. Former WIRED reviewer Adrienne So loved the Submarine version of the V15, and I've been really impressed by the V16's version as well.

If you hate emptying your cordless vacuum, there's an add-on for that, too. You can buy the V10 Konical now with Dyson's new Auto-emptying Dok that can hold up to 60 days of debris. It's a great add-on I've tried with other vacuums like Shark and Tineco and loved because it keeps my vacuum charged and upright, and it stores accessories as well. Dyson has mentioned launching one of these for the V16 in the future, but I'm not sure when that could come to fruition.

If I were to assign points based on these, the V16 Piston Animal ties with the Gen5Detect after getting its add-on while the Gen5Detect has none since it has neither of these additions, and once its own docking station arrives it would pull into first. The V10 Konical remains close behind. It's up to you whether these add-ons make it worth buying, or if you want to choose the models that actually performed best for what you need vacuumed most.
